title: Brand Profile
description: The client's approved theme, voice and channel specifications. Authored once per client and reused across changes. `approval` is the mechanical form of the never-build-a-lookalike rule: apply_brand.py and qa_comms.py both hard-fail when it is unpopulated.

source.description: There is deliberately no 'inferred' value. A palette nobody approved is a lookalike, and this schema will not record one.

scope.description: What was approved — e.g. 'internal employee comms, all channels'

approval.description: Filled by a human, always. A profile with this blank is treated as no profile at all: stop and ask.

palette.description: The named roles every producer maps onto: ink/ink_soft are heading and body text, canvas is the background, panel a tinted block. apply_brand.py emits these as deck_theme.json for the .pptx build and checks every ink/canvas pair against the WCAG floor.

palette_rules.description: Human rules a script cannot check — e.g. 'accent never on body text', 'primary only on full-bleed panels'.

web_safe_fallback.description: What a producer falls back to when the brand typeface is not installed on the machine building the artifact. A .docx or .pptx referencing an absent font substitutes silently, so name what you are willing to see instead.

tone.description: The part no extraction can produce. Always hand-written, whatever the source of the palette.

banned_words.description: Checked mechanically against every block of draft text.

preferred_terms.description: Map of avoid -> use, e.g. {"staff": "colleagues"}. Checked mechanically.

channel_specs.description: All optional; all enforced when present. A stated limit is a hard failure in Stage 4, an unstated one falls back to the channel library's default as a warning.

docx.description: Page setup shared by the email and article channels, both of which build as .docx.

dotx_path.description: Client Word template / letterhead, where one exists

canva_brand_template_id.description: The client's approved Canva Brand Template (an id beginning BTM). Present means the autofill route: get-brand-template-dataset then create-design-from-brand-template, and design_provenance becomes client-approved-template. Absent means generate-design, which invents the layout and is stamped generated-unapproved. Brand Templates live in Canva and are referenced by id — there is no file to upload — and listing them needs a Canva paid plan.

canva_brand_kit_id.description: Optional brand kit to constrain a generated design when no Brand Template exists. Also requires a Canva paid plan.

canva_brand_template_id.description: As for banner — the approved Canva Brand Template id, which switches this lane from generate-design to autofill.

edm.description: A marketing/comms-style HTML send, distinct from the direct email channel — its own subject-line convention, not inherited from email.

potx_path.description: The client's approved PowerPoint template. Absent means the from-scratch route, labelled UNAPPROVED TEMPLATE at handover.

avatar.description: Named presenter avatar, where the client has approved one

voice_name.description: Human-readable label for voice_id, e.g. 'Jacob L. - Corporate Training & Tutorial' — for review, never used to select the voice.

words_per_minute.description: Used to convert script length into an estimated runtime.

voice_name.description: Human-readable label for voice_id — for review, never used to select the voice.

voice_id.description: An ElevenLabs voice id. Must come from creative_list_voices (or a value the client itself supplied) — never invented or recalled from memory, the same never-invent rule this schema already enforces on the brand palette.

voice_provenance.description: The direct analogue of design_provenance, but for the narration voice rather than the layout. 'generated-unapproved' means a tool (creative_list_voices) picked this voice and no client has signed off on it. 'cloned-with-consent' means the voice belongs to a real, named person and requires a complete voice_consent record — qa_comms.py fails the run when one is missing, one notch stricter than the design-provenance rule because an unsubstantiated consent claim about a real person's voice must never reach production.

voice_consent.description: Required whenever voice_provenance is 'cloned-with-consent'. An unsubstantiated claim of consent about a real person's voice is a hard failure in qa_comms.py, not a warning.

person.description: The named person whose voice this is.

consent_recorded_by.description: Who captured and can vouch for the consent.
